data.description:
## Problem

`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` sits at **798 lines against the locked 800-LOC hard cap** — two lines of headroom. The next change that adds three lines to it fails CI, and there is no allowlist and no way to raise the limit (`.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked; a contributor change to it fails the build by design).

This is not hypothetical. Change 2359 (`bd66-28a4-fd31-4c9f`) already hit it: the file was 788 on main, 2359 added 45, and CI refused at 833 on all four platforms. That change landed by relocating `run_auto_maintenance` into `event_commit_git.py` and compressing a comment block — which cleared the cap but left the file at 798, so the problem is deferred rather than solved. Several other in-flight changes are growing `src/rebar` modules concurrently.

## The seam — it already exists in the file

`gitutil.py`'s own module docstring carves out a self-contained policy essay, "Blocking policy under local git lock contention". That is the boundary: **`gitutil` RUNS a git subprocess; the extracted layer DECIDES what happens when git's own locks are contended.** The dependency runs one way (`gitutil` -> `git_locking`).

The cluster moves as a unit because its members already call each other: both advisory flocks (`_store_git_op_lock`, `fetch_coordination_lock`), `_with_index_lock_retry` with its predicates/jitter/backoff, `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock`, both test probes, and `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` — the one tracker filesystem primitive every lock path anchors on.

Resulting sizes: **`gitutil.py` 373, `git_locking.py` 484** — both inside the 200-500 LOC target, leaving ~427 lines of headroom instead of 2. `gitutil` re-exports the moved names so its ~10 importers are untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gitutil.py` and the new module are each within the 200-500 LOC target and under the 800 cap; `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` passes.
- [ ] The extraction is BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING: every moved function body is byte-identical to its original, and the retained half of `gitutil.py` differs only in its docstring and import block — no executable line changed.
- [ ] The same tests pass before and after the split, with the ONLY delta being the module-size contract test flipping RED to GREEN.
- [ ] Every `monkeypatch.setattr` aimed at a moved symbol is retargeted to the new module, and each retarget is shown to be load-bearing.
- [ ] `gitutil`'s existing importers require no change (re-exports hold).

## Testing

- Compare moved line ranges against the new module with `difflib` and show the diff is empty apart from join whitespace — do not eyeball it.
- **`monkeypatch.setattr` is the dangerous part and needs explicit proof.** A patch aimed at the wrong module is **silently vacuous**, not a loud failure: the test still passes while patching nothing. For each retargeted patch, demonstrate it still takes effect — e.g. assert the patched value is observed, or seed a mutant the patch is supposed to mask and confirm the test notices. A green suite is NOT evidence here.
- Grep for the module path and every moved symbol **as a STRING** (`monkeypatch.setattr`, `getattr`, `importlib`, patch targets, docs references). An LSP cannot see these, so a semantic search returning nothing is not evidence of absence.
- Run `make lint` (including the complexity ratchet: `new=0 increased=0`) and `make typecheck` to zero, plus `check_comment_hygiene`, `check_raw_git_writes`, `check_wall_clock_asserts`.
data.title: Split _store/gitutil.py along its git-lock-contention seam: 798/800 leaves two lines of headroom
